events.headline: Murray in concussion protocol, Wentz trending toward Week 2 start at Chicago
events.detail: Murray left Sunday's opener against Green Bay after a violent hit while sliding and was placed in the NFL's concussion protocol. Coach Kevin O'Connell said Monday the team will handle his clearance day by day, while noting Murray was able to attend team meetings. Carson Wentz, who relieved him and threw three touchdowns in the 39-22 win, is expected to start Week 2 at Chicago if Murray doesn't clear the protocol in time.
events.so_what: A backup taking the reins for at least a week matters directly in a 4-point-passing-TD format with only one starting QB slot per roster -- Wentz is a streamable one-week fill if he starts, and Murray's own roster needs a contingency plan rather than assuming he clears in time for kickoff.

league_notes.hbgbs: Murray is DiaperDutyDaddy's.

events.headline: Browns' Sampson expected to miss extended time with knee injury; Sanders next up behind Judkins
events.detail: Sampson was ruled out early in Sunday's loss at Jacksonville with a knee injury and left on crutches in a brace. Coach Todd Monken said Monday the team was still evaluating the injury and expected more clarity by Wednesday, but multiple reports characterize the early outlook as more than just a Week 2 absence. Raheim Sanders, who opened the season as Cleveland's No. 3 back, is next in line for touches behind starter Quinshon Judkins.
events.so_what: Losing a backup back for an extended stretch is a bench-spot loss on the injured player's own roster in a 5-bench-spot format rather than a lineup change for Judkins, who remains the clear early-down starter -- but it makes Sanders a name worth knowing as this format's next handcuff in line if anything happens to Judkins.

league_notes.hbgbs: Judkins is Stipe's -- unaffected as Cleveland's clear starter; Sampson was never rostered here.
league_notes.pit: Judkins is BrittAndTheBoys's -- unaffected; Sampson is unrostered.
league_notes.clash: Sampson is sierragrace's, a bench-spot loss; Judkins is kimberosburn's and remains the clear starter, unaffected. Sanders is unrostered.

events.headline: 49ers rookie Black matched McCaffrey's touch count in Week 1 -- an early committee signal to track
events.detail: Rookie Kaelon Black played 28 snaps (36% of routes run) to McCaffrey's 35 snaps (56% of routes) in San Francisco's Week 1 win over the Rams, and out-carried him 14-10 while finishing with an identical 15 total touches. McCaffrey still handled the passing-down and red-zone work. Coach Kyle Shanahan hasn't announced a formal plan for how the workload splits going forward.
events.so_what: A rookie already earning a near-even carry split behind the starter is worth tracking early -- McCaffrey still holds the passing-down role that a bell-cow-preferring format like this one prices highest, but a second straight week of a 14-carry rookie would be a real value shift rather than a one-game fluke.

league_notes.hbgbs: McCaffrey is Sladsous's; Black is unrostered.
league_notes.pit: McCaffrey is trentonwest33's; Black is ColesMomPlays2Win's -- a bench stash on a different roster, not a threat to the same lineup.
league_notes.clash: McCaffrey is kimberosburn's; Black is nDabb's -- same split, two different rosters.

events.headline: Commanders TE Okonkwo exits Washington debut with hamstring injury
events.detail: Okonkwo left Sunday's 24-22 loss to Philadelphia in the third quarter with a hamstring injury and did not return, finishing with two catches for 16 yards on three targets in his first game after signing with Washington this offseason. No practice-participation update has been reported yet ahead of Week 2.
events.so_what: This format's tight end position is already thin -- a hamstring injury of unknown severity to a projected role player there is worth checking on Wednesday's practice report before locking him into a Week 2 lineup rather than assuming a clean bounce-back.

league_notes.clash: Rostered by YOU (ThatWasButtery) -- worth checking Wednesday's practice report before setting your Week 2 TE spot.

events.headline: McConkey day-to-day with rib injury after hard hit in Chargers' Week 1 loss
events.detail: McConkey was hit hard across the middle in the third quarter of Sunday's loss to Arizona and left holding his chest after finishing with 82 yards and a touchdown on five catches. Coach Jim Harbaugh called him day-to-day Monday and said the team wants to see how he progresses through the week before setting his Week 2 status against Las Vegas.
events.so_what: A day-to-day rib injury with no practice-report data yet is a genuine check-Wednesday situation in a 5-bench-spot format -- worth having a real bench or waiver alternative ready rather than assuming he clears by Sunday.

league_notes.hbgbs: Rostered by bwalsh89.

events.headline: Jaguars' Thomas expected to play Week 2 after early exit with shoulder injury
events.detail: Thomas left Sunday's blowout win over Cleveland in the second quarter with a shoulder injury but returned for Jacksonville's final drive of the first half, an encouraging sign. Coach Liam Coen said Monday he expects Thomas to play in Week 2 against Denver, likely with a limited practice week and instructions to avoid unnecessary contact rather than a hard snap-count plan.
events.so_what: A limited-practice, expected-to-play designation with no setback reported is a lean-start signal rather than a bench call in this format's WR math -- worth a final look at Friday's official tag, but the early read favors starting him over a bench alternative.

league_notes.hbgbs: Rostered by Sladsous.

events.headline: Ravens lose both Flowers (hamstring) and rookie Lane (wrist) out of Sunday's rout of the Colts
events.detail: Flowers produced 5 catches for 150 yards and a touchdown before Baltimore ruled him out in the second quarter of Sunday's 41-23 win over Indianapolis with a hamstring injury; Ian Rapoport reported Monday it is 'not considered serious' and he is considered day-to-day, with a real shot at Week 2 vs. the Saints. Separately, rookie Ja'Kobi Lane exited the same game after one catch for 11 yards and is believed to have a fractured wrist; an MRI Monday will set a firmer timeline, but multiple reports project several weeks out.
events.so_what: Flowers' injury reads as a bench-and-see call rather than a waiver scramble given the 'not serious' language, but Lane's multi-week wrist injury is a real bench-spot loss on a 5-man bench — expect more routes for Baltimore's other pass catchers over the next several weeks regardless of whether Flowers plays Week 2.

league_notes.hbgbs: Flowers is pauldag's — the same roster already down A.J. Brown, so this stacks thin at WR there. Lane is unrostered here.
league_notes.pit: Flowers is tyanserg's; Lane is ColesMomPlays2Win's — two different rosters affected, not one.
league_notes.clash: Flowers is on YOUR roster (ThatWasButtery) — with the injury called not serious, this is a bench-and-monitor situation for Week 2 rather than a waiver need yet.

events.headline: Brown's IR timeline lengthens to six weeks, not four — earliest return is Week 8
events.detail: Updates the Sept. 11 item. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport now reports Brown is expected to miss roughly six weeks with the high-ankle sprain, not the four-game minimum first reported when he landed on IR. He'll avoid surgery. Six weeks pushes his earliest eligible return to Week 6 (he's IR-eligible to activate then) with Week 8 vs. Miami the more realistic target — two weeks longer than the original CBS Sports report, and it now spans the Steelers, Jaguars, Bills, Raiders, Jets and Bears games.
events.so_what: Two extra weeks out is a bigger bench-spot commitment in a league with only 5 bench spots — Brown's own roster should stop treating this as a short-term IR stash and plan the next six weeks around Doubs and Williams rather than counting down to an October return.

league_notes.hbgbs: Brown is rostered by pauldag, who needs to fill this spot from waivers now rather than just riding out a bye. Doubs is on mfkr's roster; Williams is unrostered league-wide. Correction: Kayshon Boutte, previously noted here as a Patriots beneficiary, was traded to Houston on Aug. 24 and has nothing to do with this Patriots story anymore -- he's still on YOUR roster (ThatWasButtery), just as a Texans WR now.

events.headline: Falcons have 'no updates' on Tua or Penix entering Week 2 vs. Carolina
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 11 item. Tagovailoa's oblique strain (unrelated to the back issue from earlier camp) kept him out of Atlanta's Week 1 loss to Pittsburgh, where Cooper Rush went 12-of-22 for 143 yards, a touchdown and two interceptions filling in. Coach Kevin Stefanski said Monday the team has 'no updates' on Tagovailoa's or Michael Penix Jr.'s health entering Week 2 against Carolina, and Ian Rapoport cautioned that oblique injuries for a throwing quarterback 'generally' cost more than one week -- leaving the timeline for either QB murky three days out from Sunday. The uncertainty doesn't touch Bijan Robinson's bell-cow rushing role, but Drake London's usage still depends on which passer is under center.
events.so_what: Two days from kickoff with no clarity on either quarterback is exactly the shallow-QB-depth situation this format's scoring makes painful -- Rush remains a thin streaming option in a league this shallow at QB if he starts again, and Robinson's own roster should treat the QB question as a passing-game wrinkle for London rather than anything that touches the run game.

league_notes.hbgbs: Robinson and London are both pauldag's -- the QB uncertainty is a wash for that roster's lineup, not a start/sit call; Rush is unrostered.

events.headline: Stribling's ankle diagnosed as a deltoid sprain, expected to miss about a month
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 10 item. Further testing back in the Bay Area confirmed Stribling's ankle injury as a deltoid sprain, with multiple reports placing his timeline at roughly a month; surgery isn't currently planned but hasn't been ruled out. His Achilles remained intact, as coach Kyle Shanahan first indicated the night of the injury.
events.so_what: A confirmed month-long absence removes any near-term chance Stribling cuts into the target math at the position -- expect the extra volume this format rewards to keep funneling to Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel rather than spreading toward a rookie return anytime soon.

league_notes.hbgbs: Evans is StoneBone69's, Samuel is ENOTS's; Stribling is unrostered league-wide.

events.headline: Kamara officially inactive vs. Lions — Etienne locked in as the early-slate workhorse
events.detail: Updates the Sept. 11 item. New Orleans' official inactive list, released roughly 90 minutes before the 1pm ET kickoff at Detroit, has Kamara out with the knee injury he was questionable with all week — a full Friday practice wasn't enough to get him over the line. Kendre Miller and C.J. Donaldson are both active behind Travis Etienne, who takes over as the clear early-down and passing-down back.
events.so_what: The game-time call is resolved: Etienne is a confident bell-cow start in this format, not a hedge, and Kamara owners need a bench or waiver alternative for today rather than a lineup swap decision.

league_notes.hbgbs: Both backs remain on the same roster (DiaperDutyDaddy) — a lineup call on that one roster, not a two-team story.

events.headline: Odunze active vs. Panthers despite a full week of limited practice on the calf
events.detail: Updates the Sept. 11 item. Chicago's official inactive list confirms Odunze will play at Carolina after carrying a Questionable tag through a week where he never practiced without limitations. Coach Ben Johnson's earlier hedging did not turn into a scratch.
events.so_what: Cleared to start, but the week-long limited-practice pattern is a real efficiency/snap-count flag worth watching early in the game rather than a clean, no-doubt green light — still the right call over your bench alternative given no in-game report of a setback.

league_notes.hbgbs: Odunze is on YOUR roster (ThatWasButtery) — cleared to start.

events.headline: Bowers has a real chance to return Week 2 at the Chargers, per Schefter
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 9 item. Adam Schefter reports the Raiders believe there's a real chance Bowers returns for Sunday's (Sept. 20) game at the Chargers, just one game removed from his meniscus trim -- the team is checking in on the knee day-to-day this week rather than penciling in a longer absence. He's officially considered day-to-day, with no practice-report data yet.
events.so_what: If Bowers actually plays Week 2, this format's already-thin tight end math (league-profile.md §4) snaps back to its normal shape -- treat Mayer as a bridge option for one more week rather than a settled starter, and check Wednesday's practice report before locking a TE spot either way.

league_notes.hbgbs: Bowers is bwalsh89's; Mayer is Stipe's -- a potential TE swap back for one roster if he clears, no change for the other.

events.headline: Mahomes cleared with no injury designation, set for Monday night return vs. Broncos
events.detail: Kansas City's final Week 1 injury report carries no designation for Mahomes, who took every snap as a full practice participant Thursday and Friday. Coach Andy Reid said the earlier practice-report listings were procedural given the knee's history, not a new setback. Monday night's game at home against Denver is his official season debut, roughly nine months removed from tearing his ACL and LCL.
events.so_what: A fully undesignated practice week is the clean clearance this format's 4-point passing-TD scoring needed -- treat him as a full-workload starter for the Monday night opener rather than a rehab-limited one.

events.headline: Buccaneers rule WR Jalen McMillan, RB Sean Tucker doubtful for the opener at Cincinnati
events.detail: Tampa Bay's Friday injury report lists McMillan (knee) and Tucker (hamstring) doubtful, along with Justin Skule (oblique) doubtful and Christian Rozeboom (foot) questionable, for Sunday's game at Cincinnati. Coach Todd Bowles said neither McMillan nor Tucker suffered a setback this week -- McMillan is working back from an early-August knee injury, Tucker from a hamstring strain in the preseason finale.
events.so_what: Doubtful is a step short of a confirmed inactive, but two starting-caliber pieces trending toward sitting Week 1 pushes extra opportunity onto whichever Buccaneers do suit up -- worth checking Sunday's inactive list before locking in a fixed role for their teammates.

league_notes.hbgbs: Neither is rostered -- a target/touch-share note for Emeka Egbuka and Bucky Irving, both on YOUR roster (ThatWasButtery), rather than a waiver alert.

events.headline: Jaguars OC frames Tuten/Rodriguez as a budding '1A/1B' combo; Allen now a Friday game-time call, not a doubt
events.detail: Updates the Sept. 8 item. Jacksonville OC Grant Udinski said this week that Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez Jr. are starting to 'hit their stride' in practice, describing a shared workload rather than naming a clear lead back. Tuten sat out one practice this week with an illness (expected to be fine for the opener); Rodriguez continues working back from a foot injury. LeQuint Allen progressed from a non-participant Wednesday to limited Thursday and Friday on his hip injury and carries an official Questionable tag on the final report, with coach Liam Coen calling it a game-time decision rather than the 'pleasantly surprised if he plays' language from earlier in the week.
events.so_what: An OC actively describing this as a '1A/1B' combo rather than naming a starter is exactly the shared-touch outcome this format's bell-cow-preferring scoring likes least — both backs price as low-end RB2/FLEX plays rather than one clear starter. Allen's move to a genuine game-time call (up from a likely-out read) reopens a three-way timeshare as a live Week 1 possibility rather than closing it.

league_notes.hbgbs: Tuten is your own roster.

events.headline: Cowboys RB Malik Davis done for the season after hip surgery; Abanikanda promoted to active roster
events.detail: Davis suffered a hip injury on a carted-off play during Friday's (Sept. 11) practice, had surgery Saturday, and was placed on injured reserve -- ending his 2026 season two days before the opener. Executive VP Stephen Jones had called it a 'pretty serious injury' before the surgery confirmed the timeline. Javonte Williams remains Dallas' starter and is unaffected; Emari Demercado (an in-season waiver claim from Kansas City) moves up as the primary backup, with practice-squad call-up Israel Abanikanda now the active-roster RB3.
events.so_what: With only 5 bench spots, a backup back going down for the year is a depth-chart event on his own roster rather than a starting-lineup change -- Dallas' lead-back workload doesn't move, but Demercado and Abanikanda are each a notch closer to relevant touches if anything happens to the starter.

league_notes.hbgbs: Davis was on mfkr's bench, the same roster that owns Jeremiyah Love -- a real bench-spot loss, not a top-of-roster one. Demercado and Abanikanda are both unrostered league-wide.

events.headline: Raiders sign TE Michael Mayer to three-year, $45M extension as he steps into the starting role
events.detail: Las Vegas signed Mayer to a three-year extension worth $45 million ($30 million guaranteed, $15 million APY) on Saturday -- the first Raiders rookie-deal extension since Hunter Renfrow in 2022. The deal lands as Mayer is set to start Sunday's opener against Miami with Brock Bowers out for a meniscus procedure; the Raiders' offense is expected to run regular two-tight-end sets regardless, so Mayer projected for real snaps even before the contract news.
events.so_what: This format's thin tight-end math (league-profile.md §4) already had Mayer projected for a real Week 1 role with Bowers out -- the new money is a long-term-commitment signal, not an added source of Week 1 targets on top of that.

league_notes.hbgbs: Mayer is Stipe's -- a real Week 1 start for that roster's TE spot, not a waiver-wire add.

events.headline: Bears sign Swift to three-year, $33.75M extension two days before the opener
events.detail: Chicago and D'Andre Swift agreed to a three-year contract extension worth $33.75 million, including $27.5 million guaranteed, signed two days ahead of the Sept. 13 opener at Carolina. Swift is coming off a career year (1,087 rushing yards, nine rushing touchdowns in 2025) and the deal runs through his age-30 season in 2029.
events.so_what: A three-year extension signed just before kickoff is a team-commitment signal, not a Week 1 usage change -- it locks Swift in as Chicago's back for the foreseeable future and removes any offseason flight risk, but it doesn't itself move his role, touches, or scoring line this week.

league_notes.hbgbs: Rostered by Sladsous -- a bench-security signal for that roster, not an action item.

events.headline: Nabers officially Questionable for Sunday Night vs. Dallas — full practice two straight days, decision is his own
events.detail: Updates the Sept. 7 item. Nabers carries a Questionable tag on Friday's final report but went through his second straight full practice with no listed limitations on his surgically repaired knee (ACL/meniscus, torn Week 4 last year) — a step past the no-contact-jersey milestone reported Sept. 7. He's still declining to guarantee he suits up, saying he won't force it if the knee isn't right, and the Giants have left the final call to him rather than making it for him.
events.so_what: Two full, unlimited practices on a Questionable tag is about as good a signal as this format gets before an actual game-day inactive list — lean toward starting him, but this is a genuine check-Sunday-morning situation for the Sept. 13 Sunday Night opener at Dallas given it's entirely the player's own call, not a medical clearance question.

league_notes.hbgbs: Rostered by StoneBone69.

events.headline: Love officially a Friday game-time decision, coach says he's 'trending well' for his NFL debut
events.detail: Updates the Sept. 10 item. Arizona's Friday injury report lists Jeremiyah Love as a game-time decision on the high-ankle sprain, with coach Mike LaFleur telling reporters he is 'trending well' ahead of Sunday's (Sept. 13) opener at the Chargers. No corresponding practice-participation upgrade has been reported yet. James Conner remains on IR; Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight are next in line if Love sits.
events.so_what: Moving from 'battling a high-ankle sprain' to an official Friday game-time decision, with a coach calling him 'trending well,' tightens the outlook without resolving it. Love stays unstartable off a 5-man bench until he actually takes the field Sunday, with Allgeier and Knight the fallback if he's a late scratch.

league_notes.hbgbs: Love is mfkr's, Allgeier is ENOTS's; Conner and Knight are unrostered league-wide.

events.headline: Brooks cleared with 'no limitations' Friday; Canales spells out the exact committee mechanics
events.detail: Updates the Sept. 8 item. Brooks was a full practice participant Friday and is off Carolina's injury report entirely for Sunday's (Sept. 13) opener vs. Chicago, coach Dave Canales confirming 'no limitations' after three straight limited sessions with groin soreness. Canales also detailed how the split will actually work: 'we'll definitely roll it out just the way we have been -- where you have a lead back for the series, the other guy comes in on third down so they can be in there for the protection... whoever the lead guy for the base downs is, they'll get the bulk of that rhythm.' Hubbard remains the presumptive lead if healthy.
events.so_what: A coach spelling out the actual mechanism -- one back for the base-down series, the other in for third-down protection and change-of-pace work -- is more useful for a Week 1 lineup than a bare 'committee' label, and Brooks clearing Friday with no limitations removes the injury variable entirely. Expect a real Week 1 timeshare from the opening series rather than a clean bell-cow start for either back in this format's scoring.

league_notes.hbgbs: Hubbard is ENOTS's, Brooks is StoneBone69's -- this splits value across two different rosters, not one.

events.headline: Darnold likely to miss Week 2 with hip injury after leaving opener; Lock takes over as Seattle's starter
events.detail: Darnold left Wednesday's (Sept. 9) season opener against New England after one series with a hip injury, sacked on just his sixth snap. Tests ruled out a fracture, and coach Mike Macdonald described it as more of a muscle issue than a structural one. Darnold is now expected to miss next week's game at Arizona; Drew Lock relieved him and finished the win, throwing for 187 yards and a touchdown.
events.so_what: A backup taking over at quarterback for at least a week is exactly the kind of change this format's 4-point passing-TD scoring and thin one-QB depth reward tracking closely — Lock is a viable one-week streamer off waivers, and Seattle's pass-catchers carry a real efficiency question until Darnold's return date firms up.

league_notes.hbgbs: Neither is rostered; Seattle's Jaxon Smith-Njigba (ENOTS) is the pass-catcher most exposed to the QB change.
